stemMarkdown: The price of an article is first increased by 22%, and then the new price is decreased by 44%. What is the net percentage change in price? (Enter a negative value if it is a net decrease.)
solutionMarkdown: Take the original price as 100. After a 22% increase: $100 \times (1 + 22/100) = 122.00$. After a 44% decrease on 122.00: $122.00 \times (1 - 44/100) = 68.32$. Net change $= 68.32 - 100 = -31.68\%$.
altSolutionMarkdown: Shortcut formula: net \% change $= p_1 - p_2 - \dfrac{p_1 p_2}{100} = 22 - 44 - \dfrac{968}{100} = -31.68\%$.
